Definition: properly (abstractly) spontaneity, or (adjectively) spontaneous; also (concretely) a spontaneous or (by inference, in plural) abundant gift
BiblicalUsage: For the work of the tabernacle the children of Israel bring a willing offering to the LORD, and the law calls the voluntary offering what a man brings of his own heart. The freewill offerings are carried into the house, and Kore is set over the freewill offerings of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the willing offering is the truest measure of the heart: no one is forced to bring it, and the house of God is built on what His people give freely. My giving shows what I love, and God counts the free gift above the forced one.
